brief: Per Goldman's Quinn, speculative investors have sold $19.5bn of gold over five consecutive weeks since September 22, with selling accelerating into late October. Oct 20-27 alone saw $8bn in net selling, $5.2bn from long liquidation and $2.8bn from fresh shorts. Gold broke below $4,000 support on Friday and fell 1.6% during Oct 20-27 despite an 11bp decline in US 10-year real yields, a traditionally bullish driver it is ignoring. The note calls this a positioning-driven market. GS flags that other gross longs remain above their two-year median despite the liquidation, so further technical deterioration could trigger another selling wave irrespective of real yields. Flows, not fundamentals, could drive the next leg lower. Gold lost another 4.3% between Oct 27-30 as options traders increasingly bid downside protection, with three-month implied volatility and put skew rising, 25-delta put-call skew reaching the 85th percentile of its one-year range, making the correction increasingly a volatility story. The note's conclusion: gold is crashing even as equity volatility surges, undercutting its reputation as a reliable fear hedge.
